newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks steady in busy blue-chip trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks steady in busy blue-chip trade.

text.p: The official Jordanian stock market index rose marginally on Saturday in busy trade marked by blue-chip gains.

Arab Bank and Jordan Islamic Bank, both expected to gain from plans to scrap foreign ownership ceilings, maintained last week's gains. Arab Bank rose half a dinar to 264 dinars while Jordan Islamic climbed 0.02 to 3.8 dinars.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.03 percent to 161.70 points in trade worth 1.43 million dinars ($2 million).
Demand for the banks' shares swelled last week when the government announced it planned to lift the 50 percent foreign ownership limit.
Foreigners already have a 50 percent stake in both banks and the planned amendment, still to be approved by cabinet, would free up more shares for international buyers.

Jordan Cement Factory, Saturday's busiest stock, closed unchanged after trade worth nearly 700,000 dinars ($990,000). Other blue-chip stocks in demand included Jordan Phosphate Mines, which rose 0.04 dinars to 4.04 dinars.
Overall 17 shares fell and 14 rose on Saturday, while another 11 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.15 percent to 81.16 points, 2.68 percent down from the start of the year.
